subject: bismuth crystal
title: This Metal Is Radioactive, but It Will Outlive the Universe a Billion Times

scenes.text: This metal is radioactive. You could still hold it forever.
It's bismuth, the metal that grows into those rainbow staircase crystals.
For centuries it was called stable. Then in 2003, French physicists caught its atoms decaying.
Its half-life is about twenty billion billion years.
The universe is only 13.8 billion years old. That's over a billion times longer.
So yes, it's radioactive. It just never gets around to it.

description:
Bismuth was long thought to be the heaviest stable element, until a team in Orsay, France measured its alpha decay in 2003.
Its half-life is about 2 times 10 to the 19th years, more than a billion times the age of the universe.
Would you keep a radioactive crystal on your desk?
first_comment: A team in Italy re-measured it in 2012 and got the same answer: about 20 quintillion years. Which element should we look at next?
